on-field-night.displayName: Pale Print on the night field

on-accent-night.displayName: Press Black on the night action box

display.purpose: The home hero headline only, on the canary field: condensed black, 44px to 88px.

headline-page.purpose: The h1 of every page head printed on the field; method and landing pages run to 64px.

headline.purpose: A plain h1 off the field.

headline-section.purpose: The h2 under a 2px part rule.

title.purpose: h3, the finding title (780) and step titles.

body.purpose: Running text in the system face; prose runs at 1.7 with a 70ch measure.

lede.purpose: The muted paragraph under a page or section title, at most 60ch.

body-sm.purpose: Controls, tables, ledgers, notices; finding rows open to 1.65.

label.purpose: Every printed caption, in uppercase: margin labels, column heads, counters, ledger keys, cell labels.

label-field.purpose: The sentence-case caption printed above a form control.

button.purpose: Buttons, tabs, stepper and segmented options; nav links at 650.

chip.purpose: Severity, verdict, status and tone chips, in uppercase.

stamp.purpose: The rubber-stamp verdict, in uppercase; the hand-stamped severity is 14px at width 72%.

code.purpose: Code blocks with ligatures off; file references and hashes at 12px and 500.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Cards, rows, tables and sheets at rest: paper lies flat.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Loose panel: a tool panel, the at-a-glance box, the one-time token box, a raised card or finding.

shadows.name: shadow-slip
shadows.purpose: Loose sheet: the hero report slip and a glowing finding card.

shadows.name: backdrop
shadows.purpose: The backdrop behind a modal dialog.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default easing: panels rising, accordions opening, the chevron turning, dialogs.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The stamp landing and the pen strike on the slip.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and border changes on every control.

motion.name: t-panel
motion.purpose: A step panel or result block fades in and rises 6px; accordion height.

motion.name: t-dialog
motion.purpose: A dialog fades in from 98% scale, and out again.

motion.name: t-stamp
motion.purpose: A stamp lands large and light (scale 1.55, transparent), dips to 0.96 at 55%, then presses flat at its tilt.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: Children of a list enter one after another (the first eight); finding rows rise 40ms apart while the margin rule draws down.

motion.name: stamp-tilt
motion.purpose: The verdict stamp’s tilt: -4deg on the slip; the severity stamp is -3deg.

motion.name: slip-sequence
motion.value: strike 260ms at 380ms; Medium 420ms at 660ms; verdict 480ms at 1000ms
motion.purpose: The home slip’s one authored moment, off under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: wordmark
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the header keeps the mark and drops the wordmark.

breakpoints.name: grid-2
breakpoints.purpose: Equal grids go to two columns; the stepper sits inline; dialogs widen their padding.

breakpoints.name: ledger
breakpoints.purpose: Below it finding and sheet captions move above their content and stack tables read as blocks.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Section padding grows to 72px; form controls drop to 14px; the home steps go to three columns and the plans to two.

breakpoints.name: footer
breakpoints.purpose: The footer goes to four columns.

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the nav becomes a second header row that scrolls sideways.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.purpose: Split panes, three and four column grids, the two-column home hero and dossier.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: The landing hero split and the tool input and result split.

narrative.overview:
A finding goes through inspection before a triager ever sees it, and the site is that office's paperwork. Pages are forms printed in black on bond paper and canary stock: ruled fields, square corners, a part rule over every section, ledger tables with condensed caps for column heads. The review's decision comes back as a rubber stamp in ink, pressed on the draft at a slight tilt, and the one action the hunter takes prints as a solid box. Code is evidence, so it is pasted onto the form on carbon indigo, in a face that keeps every character distinct.

The density is that of a working form, not a brochure: captions in the margin, hairlines between rows, tabular figures, help printed under the control instead of hidden in a tooltip. Colour carries meaning before mood. Violet is stamp ink and means observed in the supplied files; ochre means still unproven; canary is stock, marking the page head, where you are and what you chose. Dark is the night shift of the same office: carbon indigo paper, pale print, lilac ink and canary for what you act on. The report slip stays paper, and code and the footer stay carbon, in both themes.

Motion is clerical and brief: colour changes in 120ms, panels rise 6px in 180ms, lists stagger 40ms apart. There is one authored moment, the stamp, which lands large and light and presses flat at its tilt. The confirmed anti-reference is the category's dark code-card hero: pages open on the field, and code appears as cited evidence inside a form.
keyCharacteristics: Every page head prints on the field, full width under the header rule: canary by day, lifted carbon at night.
Archivo condensed caps for margin captions, column heads, chips and stamps; the system face for running text; mono only for code and typed entries.
Stamps, not pills: verdicts and severities print in ink outline and ink letters, and the large ones are tilted rubber stamps with their own inked impression.
Square corners (2px, 3px on dialogs), 1px ink frames, hairlines inside, a 2px part rule over every section and under every table head.
Paper lies flat; only the hero slip, a raised panel and a dialog cast a shadow.
Two evidence inks, violet for observed and ochre for unproven, and a dashed line wherever something was not supplied.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Violet means observed in the supplied files, or an objection resolved; ochre means unproven: an open objection, a missing artifact, a test not run. No other colour carries evidence, and neither is spent on decoration.

rules.name: The Solid Action Rule
rules.body: The action you take is the only solid box: Press Black by day, canary at night. Every other button is a ruled box that fills with ink under the pointer.

rules.name: The Canary Is Stock Rule
rules.body: Canary fills; it never prints as letters or lines on paper. It is the field, the current nav item, the current step, the chosen option, a selection, the Operator plan. Only on carbon does it print: the footer's column titles and link hovers, and on the night shift the action box, the focus ring and the field's part rules. Anything set on canary prints in day ink in both themes.

rules.name: The Width Is Rank Rule
rules.body: The narrower and heavier the cut, the louder the line: stamps at 68%, the hero at 72%, page heads at 76%, chips at 78%, labels at 85%, headings at 88%, controls at 90%, and running text in the system face. There is no second display face.

rules.name: The Condensed Caps Rule
rules.body: Every caption printed in a margin, a column head or a chip is Archivo in condensed caps. Mono is never a label: it is for what was typed or computed, such as code, paths, file references, hashes, model ids and the dater.

rules.name: The Part Rule
rules.body: A 2px printed rule opens every section, heads every ledger and table, and underlines the site header, the dialog head and the slip's head; a 1px hairline divides inside. Nothing sits above a heading but that rule: no eyebrow, no kicker, and a breadcrumb prints only from three levels deep.

rules.name: The Field Opens The Page Rule
rules.body: Every page head prints on the field, full width, directly under the header rule. A page never opens on a bare paper column or a dark code card.

rules.name: The Loose Sheet Rule
rules.body: Paper lies flat. A shadow means a sheet laid over the form: the hero slip over its pink carbon copy, a raised tool panel, a dialog. It is never hover feedback, and never on a resting card.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Blank Rule
rules.body: A dashed line is a field left blank or a sheet that is not real: an unrated severity, Hold: duplicate, unsupplied code, an evidence gap, the frame around invented output. It is never decoration.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius and duration from the tokens in `web/public/css/base.css` section 1. A new state colour goes into all three theme blocks (day, night by preference, night by choice), and a test keeps the two night blocks identical.
Do open every page on the field and every section with the 2px part rule.

Do print margin captions, column heads, chips and stamps in Archivo condensed caps (12px, width 85%, 680 to 720, 0.07em), and keep mono for code, paths, references, hashes, model ids and typed entries.
Do carry a row's standing in its caption's ink, violet for observed and ochre for unproven, beside one neutral 1px margin rule that turns dashed where something was not supplied.

Do print verdicts and severities as stamps (an ink outline, ink letters, a trace of fill), give a large verdict its inked impression, and re-run `scripts/build-stamps.mjs` when a label, the stamp geometry or the font changes.
Do keep code on carbon indigo in both themes, with observed lines in violet and unproven lines in ochre.
Do put invented output in a dashed frame labelled Example.
Do keep every touch target at 44px, every text at 12px or more, and form controls at 16px under 768px.
Do honour reduced motion: transitions and animations stop, the running bar becomes a solid line and skeletons go flat.
donts: Don't put anything above a heading: no eyebrow, no kicker, no two-level breadcrumb.
Don't mark status with a coloured stripe on the edge of a card, ledger row, tab, list item or fact panel; the ink of the caption carries it.
Don't set captions, column heads or buttons in mono, or add a second display face; Archivo is the one webfont, and it is self-hosted.
Don't round a corner past 3px or draw a pill; the stamp's em corner is the only soft one (the brand mark keeps its own tile), and circles are kept for marks: dots, radio marks and the spinner.
Don't shadow a resting card, row or table, or lift anything on hover; shadows belong to the slip, raised panels and dialogs.
Don't fake ink with a shared, repeating noise tile or a texture overlay; each stamp carries its own impression.
Don't dress a tool or code panel as a terminal window; a tool panel opens with a form head (the form's number, its name and a tag in condensed caps on the Office-Use Shade over a 2px rule).
Don't lead a page with a dark code card; the page head prints on the field and code appears as cited evidence inside a form.
Don't add a hex value outside the token blocks, an inline style, or a font or image from another origin; the CSP blocks them and the build fails.
Don't nest cards, or hide help in a tooltip.
